description: Two adjacent equal highs. The doctrine's tie rule must confirm the LAST member of the equal set, never the first.
labelling_rationale: SLS §3.1 equal-extreme rule: when strict inequality fails only because a window candle is within epsilon of H[s], no swing confirms yet; the last candle of the equal set that is subsequently followed by k strictly lower highs becomes the confirmed swing point. Highs are [10, 11, 15, 15, 11, 10, 9] with k_int = 2, so indices 2..4 are evaluable. Index 2 (H=15) is immediately followed by index 3 at the same 15, so it does NOT have k strictly lower highs on its right and must be rejected — this is the half of the rule that a naive implementation gets wrong by confirming the first equal high. Index 3 (H=15) has 11 and 15 to its left (nothing higher, and the 11 is strictly lower, satisfying the requirement that the window is not flat) and 11 and 10 to its right, both strictly lower, so it confirms at price 15. Index 4 (H=11) is dominated by the 15s. Lows are [9, 10, 14, 14, 10, 9, 8]: index 2 and 3 both have a strictly lower low to their left, and index 4 has a strictly lower low to its right, so no swing low confirms. Seven candles is below the 11 needed for k_ext = 5, so external swings are empty; with one swing high there is no same-kind predecessor to classify against (§3.3), and §3.4 leaves the trend RANGING.
